updatedBySignals.change: Incident answer rewritten to use only LastPass's published statements, with links.
Price line updated: 1Password Business is $8.99 per user per month, billed yearly.
Added an MSP question about managing clients.

quickDismiss: 1Password is a good product with a higher price. LastPass Business is $7 per user against 1Password's $8.99, with 24/7 phone support, and it's built so non-technical staff use it from day one.

whereWeWin.detail: Teams Starter Pack stops at 20 users. After that it's Business at $8.99 per user per month, billed yearly. LastPass Business is $7.
whereWeWin.proof: At 120 users that's $12,946 a year for 1Password Business against $10,080 for LastPass Business, at list prices.

whereWeWin.detail: LastPass's own comparison says it's designed so employees can start with little to no training. Adoption is what the business buyer is paying for.
whereWeWin.proof: Harbor & Pike CPAs: 96% of staff active in 30 days, with no training sessions (sample customer).

whereWeWin.detail: LastPass Business includes 24/7 phone, email, and live chat. LastPass says 1Password support runs business hours with no 24/7 phone option; confirm that with the buyer rather than asserting it.
whereWeWin.proof: Show where an admin starts a phone support case from the Admin Console.

whereTheyWin.point: The security lead trusts their record more
whereTheyWin.handle: Don't compete on history. Get the security lead a meeting before the proposal, send the incident posts and certification list, and offer a security review with an SE.
1Password sells SSH, CLI, and device trust tools. If the buyer needs those, say so plainly and qualify the deal early. Most 50 to 500 person buyers are buying a password manager.

landmines: "Once you pass 20 people, which 1Password plan will you be on, and what's the per-user price?"
"Who on your team will need help on a weekend, and how will they reach support?"
"How will your non-technical staff learn the tool? Is training in your rollout plan?"
"If you manage passwords for other companies, how will you see all your clients in one place?"

objections.objection: "LastPass had a breach. Why would we trust you with our passwords?"
objections.response: Don't dispute it, and don't add detail. Say what LastPass has published: in 2022 an attacker copied a backup of customer vault data. Passwords and notes in it were encrypted; URLs were not. LastPass says it never stores or knows the master password. Since then, LastPass says it rebuilt its infrastructure on a new cloud platform, rotated secrets and certificates, changed privileged access controls, raised PBKDF2 to 600,000 iterations, and added ISO 27701 to ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, and BSI C5. If they ask about 2026: the June incident was at a vendor, Klue, and LastPass says customer vaults were not affected. Then send these links and offer the security review.

1Password lists ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, and 27701 plus SOC 2. LastPass lists ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, and BSI C5. Ask which certifications their compliance team requires, then send the matching reports through the security review.

objections.objection: "1Password's Secret Key makes it more secure."
objections.response: Don't argue design. Explain ours in plain terms: LastPass encrypts and decrypts the vault on the user's device with AES-256, and derives the key from the master password with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 600,000 iterations. For anything deeper, bring in an SE. Never improvise on cryptography.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: How fast the rollout goes and how much they'll maintain.
byPersona.lead: Directory integrations with Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, OneLogin, and Active Directory on Business, and 100+ policies.
byPersona.avoid: Talking about 1Password's provisioning patches. It reads as cheap.
byPersona.proofPoint: Sample customer Harbor & Pike went live in 9 days with Entra ID sync.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: Encryption model, audit logs, certifications, and the incident history.
byPersona.lead: The incident answer, word for word, with links. Then the certification list and SIEM integration with Splunk and Microsoft Sentinel.
byPersona.avoid: Saying the incident "wasn't a big deal" or adding detail that isn't in LastPass's posts.
byPersona.proofPoint: Offer a security review with an SE and the compliance reports.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: Price per user and whether staff will use it.
byPersona.lead: $7 against $8.99 at their seat count, plus 24/7 phone support.
byPersona.avoid: Leading with features. Lead with cost and adoption.
byPersona.proofPoint: Cost math at their seat count.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: Autofill that works and nothing new to learn.
byPersona.lead: Show the browser extension saving and filling a login in the demo.
byPersona.avoid: Admin screens in a demo for end users.
byPersona.proofPoint: Sample customer Harbor & Pike: 96% active in 30 days.

updatedBySignals.change: New answer to Bitwarden's "$6 vs $7" comparison.
Added the LastPass Enterprise migration guide.
Added a question about apps outside the vault.

quickDismiss: Bitwarden is cheaper and open source, and technical teams like it. LastPass is built for the whole company: SSO and 100+ policies on Business, phone support, and an app non-technical staff can use without training.

whereWeWin.point: SSO and policies without the top plan
whereWeWin.detail: Bitwarden puts SSO, enterprise policies, and account recovery on Enterprise ($6). Teams ($4) leaves them out. LastPass Business ($7) includes directory integrations, federated login, and 100+ policies.
whereWeWin.proof: At 120 users: Bitwarden Enterprise $8,640 a year, LastPass Business $10,080. The gap is $1,440 a year, at list prices.

whereWeWin.detail: Bitwarden's pricing page lists priority 24/7 email support. LastPass Business includes 24/7 phone, email, and live chat.
whereWeWin.proof: Show an admin opening a phone support case.

whereWeWin.detail: LastPass's own comparison describes Bitwarden as built for technical teams and LastPass for small and midsize businesses, including non-technical users.
whereWeWin.proof: Cedar Valley Health Billing switched from Bitwarden after front-office staff kept saving passwords in spreadsheets (sample customer).

whereTheyWin.handle: Agree. Then make sure they compare the same plan, and price the time IT spends supporting staff who don't adopt the tool.
If the buyer requires self-hosting, LastPass isn't a fit; LastPass describes itself as closed-source and cloud-based. Qualify that early and move on.

whereTheyWin.point: An easy path off LastPass at renewal
whereTheyWin.handle: Bitwarden publishes a migration guide for LastPass Enterprise customers. CS leads renewals with adoption numbers before price comes up.

landmines: "Which Bitwarden plan is your quote on? Does it include SSO and admin policies?"
"When someone in accounting gets locked out on a Saturday, how do they get help?"
"What will you see about apps your team uses that were never saved in the vault?"
"Who will train non-technical staff, and how long do you expect adoption to take?"

objections.objection: "LastPass had a breach. Why would we trust you with our passwords?"
objections.response: Don't dispute it, and don't add detail. Say what LastPass has published: in 2022 an attacker copied a backup of customer vault data. Passwords and notes in it were encrypted; URLs were not. LastPass says it never stores or knows the master password. Since then, LastPass says it rebuilt its infrastructure on a new cloud platform, rotated secrets and certificates, changed privileged access controls, raised PBKDF2 to 600,000 iterations, and added ISO 27701 to ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, and BSI C5. If they ask about 2026: the June incident was at a vendor, Klue, and LastPass says customer vaults were not affected. Then send these links and offer the security review.

objections.objection: "Bitwarden is $6 everything included. You're $7 plus add-ons."
objections.response: "Those are their numbers, and they're right. Let's compare the same thing. $6 is Bitwarden Enterprise; Teams at $4 leaves out SSO and policies. LastPass Business at $7 includes directory integrations, federated login, 100+ policies, and 24/7 phone support. SaaS Monitoring is the add-on, on Business Max at $11, and only if you need it."

objections.objection: "Open source means anyone can check Bitwarden's security."
objections.response: True, and it matters to some teams. LastPass's answer is third-party audits and certifications: ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, BSI C5, and ISO 27701. Offer the reports through the security review.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: Control, scripting, and not babysitting users.
byPersona.lead: Policies scoped to users, groups, or the whole company, and directory sync on Business.
byPersona.avoid: Dismissing open source. Many IT admins value it.
byPersona.proofPoint: Sample customer Cedar Valley: help desk password tickets down 60%.

byPersona.lead: The incident answer with links, then certifications and SIEM integration.
Plan-for-plan cost at their seat count, then adoption.
byPersona.avoid: Pretending the price gap doesn't exist.
byPersona.proofPoint: Cost math at their seat count.

byPersona.theyCareAbout: Managing many clients and billing them cleanly.
byPersona.lead: LastPass's multi-client dashboard and per-client billing reports.
byPersona.avoid: Claims about Bitwarden's provider portal we haven't checked.
byPersona.proofPoint: Sample partner Northgate IT runs 34 client accounts from one dashboard.

quickDismiss: Keeper's recent announcements aim at government and regulated buyers. For a 50 to 500 person company that needs a password manager its staff will use, show a fast rollout and real adoption: Summit Dental went live across 22 offices with Okta (sample customer).

whereWeWin.detail: Keeper lists SIEM integration and compliance reporting as add-ons. LastPass Business includes advanced reporting and SIEM integration with Splunk and Microsoft Sentinel.
whereWeWin.proof: Show the advanced reports and SIEM settings in the Admin Console.

whereTheyWin.handle: Keeper claims FedRAMP High and GovRAMP. If the buyer needs those, qualify out early.

landmines: "Which features in your Keeper quote are add-ons, and what do they cost?"
"Do you need FedRAMP, or a password manager your staff will use?"
